title: Need help with Generator Parts Rpg maker mz

posts.author: spades141
posts.body:
I download some dwarf parts that are made to make my own look for dwarfs in the mine. which i thought is cool. however, i watched a video about how to put them into the file.
is the video i watched. it says that all the files need to be named something like this FG_Clothing1_p25_c1, FG_FrontHair_p01_c1_m003, etc. well these dwarf images i got are not in said format. there is 185 pictures and they are all just ears_01, Beard_01, etc etc. do i have to change all the names like FG_Beard_p01_c1_m003 but change the po1 to p60 or some number different. i also have question about pre made sprite assets. i see a few on itch.io but if i buy those do i just have to post them into the file needed or will i have to change abunch of names like i do in generator. also if they are made for mv will they work for mz.
https://everlywritesgames.itch.io/nine-realms-nidavellir-dwarves-pack
is what i was look at. please and thank you. you guys are very helpful to newbs. ive posted a good bit in the last few weeks and i am sorry lol

posts.author: Avery
posts.body:
Some text formatting goes a long way. Basically, first of all, yes, you need to correctly format the names of the pieces so the generator knows what to do with them.
Since you are a beginner and seem to work on getting the basics going for yourself, I'd say no, you cannot make MV parts work in MZ. Technically one can, but it is fiddly, requires a deeper understanding of the generator and willingness and skill to do certain (sometimes extensive) edits in a graphic program like Gimp. I have a tutorial about that, but I don't think as of now it is of much help to you:
https://www.rpgmakerweb.com/blog/can-we-use-mv-generator-parts-in-mz
The sprites you linked are not even the default generator style, so there is absolutely no way you can get them running in the default MZ generator.
Things you can do:
Use adult sized sprites with beards and helmets and have a (maybe funny) ingame explaination on why dwarves in this world aren't "fun sized". Or maybe only in that one town.
Make the dwarves using the kid generator - you can then use the adult male beards and edit them on and boom:
Looks like a regular kid, right? Well, since we talk NPC, we ignore the SV, that is the most time consuming anyways.
Then, make a face, ignore how the char and SV look, you only want a face that matches your char well enough to pass:
You now have those two files:
And all that's left is to add the beard to the "child". Open the graphic in Gimp (it is free).
Get the TV (charset piece of the beard) and open it, too.
Paste the bead onto a new layer on the "child" - the head size is the same, you just need to move the layer down a bit cause the child is shorter.
Then, step 1, you remove all parts of the beard that are covered by the hair. That you do by selecting your char layer and use select by color with a tolerance of 0 and all shades of the hair one by one. Then you select the beard layer, and with an eraser with a hard edge remove all the beard parts that overlap hair that is in front of it (some will also overlap with back hair behind it, so just pressing delete is not a solution. But this is a matter of a few minutes at most).
Before
After
Then you recolor the beard to match. To do so, folow this tutorial I made:
Recoloring Pixel Art
Can you make proper recolors?  Yes No What do you mean with “proper”?   While dedicated beginners as 15 year old me back then are able to recolor pixelated sprites with MS Paint, that is very much noch recommended.  For this tutorial I will use Gimp, it is free, powerful and can do all the...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
Basically, you replace each color of the beard with the matching shade of the color ramp of the hair.
And then you are done:
Other option would be to e.g. to make the head you like for the adult person and then transplant it onto a child body.
Like this:
and export face and charset.
Then make a kid with a clothing that vaguely matches what you see in the face and the same skin tone and export the char:
Again, open both in Gimp and place the adult sprite on a layer on top of the child one - again, it has to be moved down a little so they match, I made it semi-transparent to show you how the eyes line up perfectly if you do it right.
With select by color and a tolerance of 0 you again select one by one all the colors of the clothing until only hair and skin and eyes remain (and a hat/helmet, if you added it). Then delete that.
The adult arms of course remain, use again a hard edged eraser to get rid of them (or e.g. box select and delete or what other way you prefer).
Technically, you can also use other methods to erase the body, like all eraser for example. what matters is that you want the whole body to be gone and the whole head + headgear to remain.
With the child body combine, voila, a dwarf:
Yes, this can be a bit tedious, probably the reason there aren't too many plug and play dwarves out there.
